questions.q: What happens to a model's internal parameters during inference?
options: They are frozen and unchanged — inference only runs a forward pass
They are reset to random values before every prediction
They are retrained on each new input
They are deleted after each prediction
questions.explain: Inference uses the model's already-trained, fixed parameters to produce an output for a new input; no training or parameter adjustment happens during inference.

questions.q: During training, what does the loop in the lesson's pseudocode actually adjust on each pass?
options: The raw training data itself
The model's parameters, nudged in the direction that reduces the measured error
The labels attached to each example
The hardware the model runs on
questions.explain: Training repeatedly compares a prediction to the known correct label, measures the error, and nudges the model's parameters to make future predictions less wrong.

questions.q: Why is a single inference call typically much cheaper and faster than training?
options: Inference uses more powerful hardware than training
Inference is one forward pass through an already-finished model, instead of millions of repeated passes with error correction
Inference doesn't require a trained model at all
Inference always runs on a different dataset than training
questions.explain: Training repeats forward passes plus error correction over huge datasets, often for days; inference is just one forward pass through parameters that are already fixed, which is why it can run in milliseconds.

questions.q: When you send a prompt to an LLM API and get a response back, which phase are you using?
options: Training, because the model learns from your prompt
Both training and inference happen equally on every request
Inference — the model's parameters were already fixed during training done earlier by its creator
Neither; API calls don't involve a trained model
questions.explain: Calling an LLM API is pure inference: the model's weights were already trained (and frozen) ahead of time, and your request is just one more forward pass through that finished model.

questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts training and inference data needs?
options: Both training and inference strictly require labeled data
Training generally needs labeled examples to learn from; inference is typically run on new, unlabeled input to get a prediction
Inference requires more labeled data than training
Neither phase requires any data at all
questions.explain: Training needs labeled examples so the model has a correct answer to compare against. Inference is applied to new input precisely because you don't already know the answer — that's why you need a prediction.
